$schema: single source of truth for the dev-page tool (dev-tools/client-config.html) and provision-client.ts. Both read this same file so the feature catalog and file/migration mapping never drift out of sync between the two tools. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-per-client-deployment-and-ai-automation-plan.md §3.5.1 #1/#3.

core.description: Always included in every generated client codebase, regardless of feature selection. Shared infrastructure every feature depends on.

erp.production.label: Production (BoM, routing, manufacturing orders)
erp.production.note: manufacturing_order (0018) references product, bill_of_materials, and location; work_order (0019) references manufacturing_order and operation (via routing, 0017) — verified via REFERENCES clauses 2026-09-05, not assumed from filenames.

erp.projects_time.label: Projects & time tracking
erp.projects_time.note: project.contact_id references the CRM contact table (design spec §8's 'contact is one record, not duplicated per module' principle), verified against migration 0020's REFERENCES clause. erp.core dependency added 2026-09-05 after the Phase 3A-4 final-review agent caught it empirically: time_entry.approval_state (0022) uses the approval_state ENUM TYPE defined in 0007/0011, which belongs to erp.core — an enum-type dependency, not a REFERENCES clause, so the original FK-only verification method for this file was structurally blind to it. erp.purchase_orders and erp.production don't need this listed explicitly since they already transitively depend on erp.core via erp.inventory, but erp.projects_time depends only on crm.contacts, so this dependency has to be explicit or provisioning a client with effort_based billing and no ERP core fails at 0022 with 'type approval_state does not exist'.

erp.sales_orders.label: Sales orders
erp.sales_orders.note: sales_order.contact_id references contact (crm.contacts); sales_order_line.product_id references product (erp.core); approval_state column uses the shared enum from erp.core (0007/0011) — verified via REFERENCES clauses and enum usage in 0023_sales_order.sql, not assumed from filenames. No app/ UI exists yet for this feature (Phase 3B ERP UI hasn't started) — files list is lib/ only, same as every other ERP feature added so far.

erp.invoicing.label: Invoicing & payments
erp.invoicing.note: invoice.sales_order_id references sales_order (erp.sales_orders); invoice.approval_state uses the erp.core enum (transitively satisfied via erp.sales_orders -> erp.core); payment.contact_id references contact (transitively satisfied via erp.sales_orders -> crm.contacts); payment_allocation.invoice_id references invoice (same feature). invoice_source_type enum also allows 'time_entries' and 'subscription' sources per 0024's CREATE TYPE, but no code path here creates an invoice from those sources yet — deferred, not a manifest gap. Verified via REFERENCES clauses in 0024_invoice.sql/0025_payment.sql.

erp.recurring_billing.label: Recurring templates & plans
erp.recurring_billing.note: recurring_template.approval_state uses the erp.core enum (0007/0011); plan.recurring_template_id references recurring_template (same feature). Verified via REFERENCES clauses and enum usage in 0026/0027. Does NOT depend on crm.contacts or erp.sales_orders — a plan/template can exist with no subscription yet.

erp.subscriptions.label: Subscriptions
erp.subscriptions.note: subscription.contact_id references contact (crm.contacts); subscription.plan_id references plan (erp.recurring_billing); subscription.approval_state uses the erp.core enum (transitively satisfied via erp.recurring_billing -> erp.core); subscription_change_event.subscription_id/previous_plan_id/new_plan_id and usage_record.subscription_id both reference subscription/plan (same feature / erp.recurring_billing). Verified via REFERENCES clauses and enum usage in 0028/0029/0030 — same discipline that caught the erp.projects_time gap. No app/ UI exists yet (Phase 3B not started); lib/ files only.

ai.tool_contract.label: AI tool contract (agent runtime)
ai.tool_contract.note: Only covers the CRM tool contract that exists today (Phase 5 scaffold). An ERP tool-contract equivalent doesn't exist yet (deployment plan §4.1.1) — add its own feature entry here once built, per §3.5.1 item 3's 'explicit declaration per new feature' decision.
